problems.title: The described cosine objective differs from released squared reconstruction loss
problems.source_location: Section 3.3, Eq. (1); Appendix C.1; models_tobo.py, forward_loss and decoder projection; engine_tobo.py training loss
claim: The method describes cosine distance between predicted and target patches, while forward_loss computes coordinate-mean squared error after optional target-only normalization.
analysis: Let a nonzero target after optional normalization be \(u\), with predictions \(z=u\) and \(z=2u\). Both have cosine distance \(0\); their squared losses are \(0\) and \(\|u\|^2/d>0\). More generally the cosine radial derivative is \(0\), whereas the squared-loss derivative at scale \(\alpha\) is \(2(\alpha-1)\|u\|^2/d\). LayerNorm precedes the unconstrained final affine projection, so it does not impose unit norm on predicted pixels. The documented training path gives the ToBo branch nonzero weight. Appendix C.1 explicitly discloses the auxiliary Siamese loss, so that branch is not an additional undisclosed change.
result: The current author paper and release optimize different reconstruction objectives. Which objective generated each published checkpoint remains unresolved; downstream performance and the token-bottleneck mechanism are not refuted.
repair: If released squared loss generated the experiments, describe the masked coordinate-mean squared error and target normalization; otherwise identify the cosine-training source and checkpoint configurations. This is a provenance-dependent proposal, not a validated retraining result.
problems.impact_rationale: The release objective and its radial gradients differ, but no reported benchmark or core architectural claim is disproved.
